newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Belarus union would not harm independence - Russian.
newsitem.headline: Belarus union would not harm independence - Russian.

text.p: Russia's deputy prime minister who co-authored a controversial draft Union Treaty with Belarus said on Monday the pact would create only a loose association that did not threaten Russia's independence.

"Some people are asking: 'In what country will we wake up on April 3?'," Valery Serov said, referring to the date on which the two countries are expected to sign the draft. "The answer is: In the very same country you went to bed."
"There will be a union of two states rather then a single state," he told a news conference.

Russian liberals and Belarus nationalists have been alarmed by the treaty, which was drafted behind closed doors by Serov, and say it could harm the independence of the two former Soviet Slav republics.
Russian President Boris Yeltsin and Belarus leader Alexander Lukashenko are expected to sign the draft on Wednesday.

Opponents of the deal have also argued that the pact's principle of "one country, one vote" was unjust in a union of two countries in which one is 15 times larger in population and economic potential.

Serov said however that the union's ruling bodies would not have much practical authority. "There is no word about the creation of any new supreme bodies that could usurp power," Interfax news agency quoted him as saying.

Serov said that the top bodies of the planned union -- the Supreme Council, Parliamentary Assembly and Executive Council -- will not get any powers stronger than they have now in a largely symbolic Russia-Belarus Community formed last April.
Yeltsin backed the draft treaty earlier on Monday but his aides did not rule out that some last minute changes could be introduced.
